target_customer: Video creators, filmmakers and studios, plus developers and enterprises that use the API for dubbing and personalized video
problem: Fixing what a speaker said or how it looked in a finished video normally means re-recording. sync. edits the mouth movement so the video matches new audio.
business_model: Usage-based API plus subscription apps (studio app, Premiere plugin, ComfyUI node), with enterprise upsell
product_category: Generative AI video, lipsync and visual dubbing

founders.name: Prady Modukuru
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a product engineer who helped launch AI cybersecurity products at Microsoft. No education listed.

education: University of Oxford, PhD (worked with Andrew Zisserman)
founders.background_notes: Co-author of the Wav2Lip research per YC page.

founders.name: Rudrabha Mukhopadhyay
founders.background_notes: Primary author of Wav2Lip per YC page.

founders.name: Pavan Reddy

founders.background_notes: YC page says he previously worked with IIIT Hyderabad on commercializing research.

technical_complexity.rationale: Training state of the art generative lipsync models and serving them at scale was hard for a small team in 2023. The founders already had the research lineage, as authors of the open source Wav2Lip, which lowered the research risk.

defensibility.rationale: Model quality and the authors' research head start were the moat. Generative video moved fast, so model advantages could erode and the company sells through an API with low switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sources found only describe these players as present in later vendor comparisons dated 2026. No acquisition of sync. was found as of this research.

market_need_then: Creators and studios spend time on re-takes and dubbing. The company's launch pitch was that video could be edited like a document. Public evidence of paid demand at the time of founding was not found beyond the Wav2Lip research reach (open source repo popularity claimed by the company).

branding.domain_note: Operates at sync.so (a .so domain). Third party directories also list a separate synclabs.so, relationship unclear.

identity.logo: Lowercase wordmark with a trailing period
identity.visual_style: Clean, product-led, film and creator oriented
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and polished, short lowercase headlines such as studio grade visual dubbing with perfect lipsync

branding.brand_signature: The lowercase name with a period and the Wav2Lip lineage
branding.community_and_virality: Company says the founders' open source wav2lip model has over 10k GitHub stars (YC page), which gave the team credibility. No merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Sources show a clear, consistent lowercase voice and the research lineage as a draw, but no press about the brand itself. The legal entity is Synchronicity Labs Inc. and the name 'sync' is common, so search confusion is likely.

outcome_analysis: sync. is active and raised a $5.5M seed led by GV in August 2024, about five months after the W24 batch. Its strength is founder market fit, since the founders authored the Wav2Lip model, and the generative video wave helped. The main risk is that lipsync becomes a feature inside larger video platforms. No later round, acquisition or shutdown was found in searches.
notes: Competitor list left empty: the only competitor sources found were vendor comparison posts dated 2026, not near the Winter 2024 batch. Wav2Lip itself is a 2020 research project from IIIT Hyderabad per the company. Funding conflicts: one tracker lists a $6M seed in July 2024 and one aggregator claims $22M total with a Series A; neither is confirmed by a primary source, so only the company-announced $5.5M seed is recorded. The seed was cross-checked only against the company's own GV announcement page and aggregators; no independent press outlet was found. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs.
